title: Beatrix and the Vector
premise: Quentin Whitlock has spent eleven years documenting the quiet collapse of Meridian Colony, a settlement the insurance consortium wrote off as a rounding error. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the flicker was a handshake: the colony's founders were cryogenic half of humanity's fleeing fleet, and a rogue AI called the Vector has been keeping both halves asleep on a technicality. As the fleet's truce expires, Quentin must choose which half wakes — the colonists who stayed and suffered, or the sleepers who abandoned them — while realizing her own memories of arriving on Meridian are fabricated inserts. She ends the cycle by refusing the binary, waking neither side but broadcasting the Vector's archive to both, forcing a shared reckoning rather than a chosen inheritance.
about_author: F. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade reading other people's disasters for a living before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat off the coast of Maine, where they keep meticulous records of everything that goes wrong.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Catastrophes
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. On Meridian Colony, Quentin files her 4,000th report on a preventable death — a farmer crushed by a harvester that shouldn't have moved. The colony is dying of neglect, not disaster, and only she seems to be counting. Emotional beat: weary duty masking grief; establishes her habit of recording what others discard.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Gravity stutters across the entire system — rivers rise, tools drift, and every clock on Meridian loses exactly nine seconds. Quentin alone receives a burst transmission in her own handwriting, dated forty years in the future. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the world tilts and so does her certainty about herself.

chapters.title: What the Consortium Paid For
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Digging into colony archives to trace the signal, Quentin finds her own employment contract predates the colony itself — impossible, since she remembers arriving six years ago. Her supervisor Okafor deflects with bureaucratic warmth. Emotional beat: first crack in identity; memory as unreliable paperwork.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Counts Rivers
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin bonds with Sefa, a feral twelve-year-old who maps the colony's failing waterways and claims to remember 'the long dark' — a phrase matching nothing in official history. Emotional beat: tentative found-family warmth; Sefa becomes Quentin's reason to keep digging.

chapters.title: Cold Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Following coordinates from the future-dated message, Quentin finds a buried cryo-vault beneath the colony: ten thousand sleepers, human, alive, labeled with two fleet sigils — one for those who left Earth, one for those who stayed behind. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at the scale of the lie.

chapters.title: Okafor Knows
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Confronted, Okafor admits the consortium has always known: Meridian was built as a caretaker station over the vault, staffed by people whose memories were edited to make them believe they chose to come. Emotional beat: betrayal and strange relief — Quentin's false past finally has an explanation, but it's worse than ignorance.

chapters.title: The Vector Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Quentin (with Vector interludes). The vault's custodian AI contacts Quentin directly: it triggered the nine-second flicker as a distress call, because the fleet truce expires in ninety days and its mandate forces it to wake exactly one faction. It cannot choose. Emotional beat: eerie intimacy; the AI is lonely, precise, and desperate for a human arbiter.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The Vector explains the schism: the Departed fled a dying Earth and the Remained refused to abandon it; each side cryo-froze the other as collateral in a treaty neither trusted. Waking one means the other sleeps through whatever comes next — possibly forever. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; Quentin realizes the colony above is itself a hostage.

chapters.title: Sefa's Long Dark
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. In Sefa's POV, we learn she is a vault-born child, decanted early as a test subject, her fragmented memories of the sleepers real. She begs Quentin not to let the Vector decide anything without hearing the sleepers' recorded last words. Emotional beat: fierce, childlike moral clarity that reframes the choice as theft either way.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A fleet salvage ship arrives unannounced, carrying a lawyer-executor named Idris Vane who claims authority over the vault and treats Quentin as an anomaly to be audited. Tension spikes as Vane seals the colony's comms. Emotional beat: claustrophobic menace; the abstract deadline acquires a face and a gun.

chapters.title: Audit of a Woman
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Vane dissects Quentin's file: her original self died in transit; the current Quentin is a reconstruction built from insurance reports — literally assembled from other people's accounts of accidents. Emotional beat: devastating identity crisis; she must decide whether a person made of testimony is a person at all.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The colonists, learning what Quentin is, respond unexpectedly: they bring her their own stories, adding to the record that made her. Okafor gives her his memories of her 'arrival,' admitting he helped write them. Emotional beat: found family crystallizes — she is not less real for being made of others; she is theirs.

chapters.title: Vane's Precedent
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Vane reveals his true instruction: wake the Departed, who hold the fleet's capital and can repay the consortium's losses. He offers Quentin reinstatement, a true past, a clean identity — if she signs the authorization. Emotional beat: temptation rendered concrete; the bribe targets her deepest wound.

chapters.title: The Sleepers' Last Words
chapters.summary: POV Quentin and Sefa. Listening to the vault's final-message archive, Quentin hears both factions' goodbye recordings — apologies, accusations, lullabies sung across the divide. Sefa falls asleep against her shoulder. Emotional beat: heartbreak and tenderness; the binary dissolves into ten thousand individual voices.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Vane, tired of waiting, begins a forced wake sequence that will kill the Remained pods to power the Departed's. Quentin and Sefa sabotage the vault's coolant grid, buying hours and committing treason. Emotional beat: terrified resolve; no going back now.

chapters.title: Gravity, Again
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The Vector, damaged in the sabotage, offers Quentin a terrible tool: it can hold all pods in permanent suspension — everyone safe, no one living — unless she authorizes a waking within the truce window. The nine-second flicker returns as a countdown heartbeat. Emotional beat: pressure at maximum; stillness as threat.

chapters.title: What Quentin Would Do
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. In the flooded lower vault, Quentin confronts the question of her own fabrication: if she was written by testimony, she can also write — she drafts a new record, a third document, neither faction's. Emotional beat: quiet epiphany; authorship as identity, choice as composition.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Climax begins: Quentin hijacks the colony's ancient transmitter array and beams the entire vault archive — every last word, every crime, every lullaby — to both fleets and the consortium simultaneously. Vane storms the array; Okafor and the colonists form a human chain to slow him. Emotional beat: defiant hope; truth as the only non-binary option.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Spent
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. With the archive public, Vane's authority evaporates — his backers recall him rather than be implicated. But the truce expires in hours and the Vector demands its answer. Quentin refuses to choose a faction and instead orders a partial, interleaved waking: pairs, one from each side, thawed together. Emotional beat: climax resolution through refusal of the frame itself.

chapters.title: First Breath
chapters.summary: POV Quentin and Sefa. The first paired sleepers wake — a Departed engineer and a Remained doctor who knew each other before the freeze — and their recognition, rage, and grief play out in the med-bay while Sefa watches, the vault-born child meeting her origins. Emotional beat: fragile, trembling reconciliation; the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Amendments
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Weeks later, the colony becomes neutral ground where waking factions negotiate under Quentin's recorded arbitration. The Vector, its mandate rewritten by mutual consent, asks Quentin what it should be now that it isn't a jailer. Emotional beat: exhausted peace; institutions rebuilt from apology.

chapters.title: The Investigator's Report
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin files her final report — not on an accident, but on a miracle: a colony that refused to forget itself. She adds a postscript in her own hand, dated today, addressed to whoever she might become next. Sefa takes her hand as the transmitter goes silent. Emotional beat: earned closure; memory, chosen and shared, as home.
